Generative AI: high-value uses

  • Variance & flux commentary from ledger and driver data
  • Board-pack first drafts: consistent, plain language, every figure linked
  • Policy & IFRS Q&A over your own accounting manual
  • Contract review: revenue, lease and covenant terms

Guardrails · the five R's
  • Restrict to approved enterprise tools
  • Reference every number to the ledger
  • Review by a qualified accountant
  • Record prompts, versions and reviewers
  • Responsibility named; the tool never signs
Module 03 · 12:30 – 12:42

Forecasting: From Point Estimates to Probabilities

Rolling, driver-based forecasts that tell the board how likely an outcome is, and when to act.

Executive
Briefing03

Live fan chart · monthly revenue (₦bn, illustrative)

—

White: actuals · gold: P50 · blue bands: P10–P90 and P25–P75 · red dashed: budget floor.

Move the drivers

—Month-12 P50 (₦bn)
—P10–P90 (₦bn)
—Chance below floor

Ask not "what will happen?" Ask "how likely, and what will we do?"

Know your drivers: 2026 oil output vs the budget (mb/d)

Total liquids. Source: 2026 Appropriation Act assumptions; H1 2026 production as reported (allAfrica, Aug 2026). Axis starts at 1.0.

The forecasting lesson

  • ≈38.4m barrels short in H1, roughly $2.49bn of gross revenue at the $64.85 budget price.
  • Monthly range 1.48–1.74 mb/d: a single-point assumption hid the volatility.
  • Your lesson: model each driver as a range, update monthly, and let the model tell you when the plan breaks.
